title: Voyager 1 Is Now One Light-Day Away. Light Needs 24 Hours to Reach It
description:
Voyager 1 is now one light-day from Earth: a radio signal moving at the speed of light needs a full 24 hours to reach it. NASA's Voyager 1 crossed that line on Nov. 18, 2026.

The numbers:
- About 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion km) from Earth, the farthest spacecraft humans have ever flown.
- Launched in 1977, still moving at about 38,000 mph.
- 24 hours for a command to get there, 24 hours for the answer to come back. NASA sends it commands about once a week.
- Its three onboard computers hold 69.63 kilobytes of memory in total, less than a single phone photo.
- On Nov. 14, 2026 it went quiet: no science or engineering data, only its carrier signal (the "hum"). As of Nov. 19, NASA engineers were analyzing the problem.

Would you keep waiting for that reply? Tell us below.

Sources:
- NASA JPL, Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth (Nov. 19, 2026): https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-voyager-1-makes-history-reaching-one-light-day-from-earth/
- Spaceflight Now, NASA's Voyager 1 is one light-day from Earth (Nov. 18, 2026): https://spaceflightnow.com/2026/11/18/nasas-voyager-1-is-one-light-day-from-earth/
- Space.com, Empire State Building glows gold for Voyager (Nov. 19, 2026): https://www.space.com/space-exploration/voyager/empire-state-building-glows-gold-for-nasas-voyager-spacecraft-space-photo-of-the-day-for-nov-19-2026
- Popular Science, Voyager's 1977 computers (69.63 KB of memory): https://www.popsci.com/science/nasa-voyager-computers-video/

Light needs a WHOLE DAY to reach it. 🚀

Voyager 1 launched in 1977. On Nov. 18 it hit one light-day from Earth: about 16.1 billion miles. Its whole memory is smaller than one selfie. Send it a message and the reply takes two days. And on Nov. 14 it went quiet: just a hum.

Would you keep waiting?

questions.q: How far away is Voyager 1 right now?
questions.a: On Nov. 18, 2026 Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth, about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion km), according to NASA JPL. It is still moving away at about 38,000 mph.

questions.q: How long does it take to send a message to Voyager 1?
questions.a: About 24 hours each way: NASA says signals now take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft and 24 hours to come back, so a reply takes about two days. The team sends it commands about once a week.

questions.q: How much memory does Voyager 1 have?
questions.a: Its three computer systems have 69.63 kilobytes of memory in total, according to Popular Science, less than a single JPEG photo from a phone.
